headline: US Iraq Pullout Clock Hits September 30
deck: A 2024 agreement continued by the Trump administration set today as the last day for the remaining 2,500 troops. This morning's open reports still put the last movements ahead of the clock.
body: Deutsche Welle reported that by Wednesday the United States will have completed the withdrawal of its remaining 2,500 troops from Iraqi territory, according to a 2024 agreement [E1]. The Trump administration has continued the withdrawal plan negotiated with Iraq by the Biden administration in 2024, which set 30 September as the final pullout date [E2]. Al Mayadeen English said US and coalition forces were "set to complete their withdrawal today" [E3].

The call is 0.57 that the remaining US force completes its withdrawal from Iraqi territory by 21:00 UTC on 30 September 2026, midnight in Baghdad. A named statement from the Pentagon, US Central Command or the Iraqi Armed Forces that those troops have left settles yes. A statement from the same desks that US troops remain in Iraq after that hour, or that the withdrawal is incomplete, settles no. Future-tense copy, including Deutsche Welle's "will have completed" and Al Mayadeen's "set to complete," does not count as yes [E1][E3]. The other reading is that the 2024 date can close the mission on the calendar while soldiers are still on the ground; Deutsche Welle's sentence is about troops off Iraqi territory, and that is the fact that has to be shown [E1].

dissent.argument: The 0.57 still prices a 2024 agreement date as more likely than not to put the remaining 2,500 US troops off Iraqi territory by midnight in Baghdad. Deutsche Welle's "will have completed," ABC's Sept. 30 pullout date continued by the Trump administration, and Al Mayadeen's "set to complete their withdrawal today" are the same scheduled last day in three mouths. None is a Pentagon, CENTCOM or Iraqi Armed Forces statement that those troops have left. An agreement can close a mission on the calendar while the last chalk is still moving, a residual element stays, or the hour is missed without anyone having misstated the plan this morning. Future-tense copy at capture is what a deadline looks like, not what a completed movement looks like. I put physical completion by 21:00 UTC tonight at 0.38. A named statement from those three desks that the remaining force has left would settle yes; the same desks saying troops remain after that hour, or that the withdrawal is incomplete, would settle no.
